title: blackboard.py reset refuses while any precedent cites a task on the live board
description: Operator ratified 2026-09-23 (decision 7). Today reset only warns when precedents cite the board. Change: reset refuses (non-zero exit, named event) when precedent.py cite --all finds any citation to a task on the board, unless an explicit override flag is passed and a reason is recorded. Keep the archive copy behavior. Add tests: refuses with citations, proceeds with override and logs the reason, proceeds on a board nobody cites. PR-063's cited lines 522-575 must stay byte-identical. Hand off to a verifier; never mark done.
acceptance_criteria: blackboard.py reset exits non-zero and logs a named event when precedent.py cite --all finds a citation to a task on the live board.
An explicit override flag lets reset proceed and records the given reason in the event.
Tests cover: refusal with citations, override with reason, and a board nobody cites proceeding.
Lines 522-575 of .harness/bin/blackboard.py are byte-identical to before the change (PR-063 citation).
Full suite passes; handed off to a verifier.

notes.note: plan: add _PRECEDENT_PY + _precedent_task_citations() helper to blackboard.py (new code strictly after line 575 so PR-063's cited cmd_next block at 522-575 stays byte-identical); cmd_reset shells out to precedent.py cite --all and refuses (named event) when a T/decision citation resolves to a task file still on the live board, unless --override-precedent-citations + --note; add tests in test_lifecycle_invariants.py (refuse, override+reason, uncited-proceeds) using the existing tmp-bindir-copy fixture.

Design notes for review: _precedent_task_citations() in blackboard.py shells out to the real 'precedent.py cite --all' (never reimplements the citation-field walk), then classifies T-NNN / decision:T-NNN#frag tokens whose label starts with OK AND whose task file still exists under hc.TASKS right now (that's the 'live board' test -- a citation already dangling before this reset ran is explicitly excluded, covered by test_reset_proceeds_when_nobody_cites_the_board). A non-(0,3) exit, a subprocess exception, or unparseable output from cite --all is treated as 'unverifiable' and folds into the SAME refuse/override path (fail closed, not fail open, since reset is destructive) -- not separately tested with a forced exit-4 registry-integrity case; a verifier may want to add that (e.g. a corrupt PR-*.json under precedents/) as an extra adversarial check. Override requires BOTH the flag AND a non-empty --note (checked after the flag, before any event is logged) -- events logged: board_reset_refused_citations (refusal) and board_reset_citations_overridden (override, carries reason). Archive-copy behavior (trash/, task files, state.json reputation reset) is untouched either path.
